label: Ricotta
note: Industry runs the same step as heat-precipitated whey protein.

about.text: Ricotta is an Italian whey cheese made from sheep, cow, goat, or Italian water buffalo milk whey left over from the production of other cheeses. However, modern ricotta is often made from milk instead of whey. Like other whey cheeses, it is made by coagulating the proteins that remain after the casein has been used to make cheese, notably albumin and globulin.

how.text: Rennet cheese leaves the whey proteins behind, so ricotta ('re-cooked') recovers them: acid and near-boiling heat together make the albumins and globulins clot. No starter culture is added; the acid comes from the whey's own lactic fermentation or from added acid.

steps.note: Hotter than for the first cheese, so the whey proteins coagulate.
Skimmed once the curd floats; acid to pH about 5.9 gives a second, coarser rise.

processing.text: Whey is left to ferment 12-24 h at room temperature for its acid, or acid is added instead. No starter is added.

facts.v: Whey left from other cheese (sheep, cow, goat, buffalo); modern ricotta is often made from milk instead, or milk added to the whey (whey pH as low as 6.1 acceptable; best from sweet whey of pH 6.4–6.5)
